primary_claim: A pipeline of six specialized LLM agents (Gemini 2.5 Pro plus Claude Code) attempting fully autonomous end-to-end scientific research succeeded on only 1 of 4 research ideas (an AI-safety semantic-entropy jailbreak-detection project, published at Agents4Science 2025), with the other 3 failing during implementation or evaluation; the authors identify 6 recurring LLM failure modes in autonomous research (training-data bias, implementation drift, memory/context degradation, overexcitement/'eureka instinct', and gaps in domain intelligence and scientific taste)

effect.metric: pipeline success rate on autonomous research ideas
effect.value: 1/4 research ideas completed the full pipeline to publication; system was rated 95% autonomous per the conference's AI Involvement Checklist

stated_future_work: Solve long-horizon coherence, research taste, and missing training/evaluation data (including records of failed attempts) as prerequisites for more autonomous science
Apply four proposed design principles (start abstract/ground later, verify everything, plan for failure and recovery, log everything) in future AI scientist systems
limitations_stated: Only four research ideas tested across three ML subdomains, no systematic ablations
Failure modes identified through observation rather than quantitative measurement
System was only 95% autonomous; humans intervened to select ideas, meta-prompt during execution, and temper overoptimistic claims during paper writing
quote: We tested our agents on 4 research ideas across ML sub-domains such as Multi-Agent RL, World Models, and AI Safety. 3 ideas failed during implementation or evaluation. Only 1 succeeded and was published at Agents4Science 2025.
